properties.name: FIELD REPORT (a work project, 2026-09-14): four hand-rolled analyses in one session, each answering a question the design held open, diagnosed "unknown" — and the conversion test run here says one of the four HAS a home that ships only in reflow2's own repo, and three have none
properties.statement:
RELAYED by Anthony from a project at his workplace, 2026-09-14; recorded without the employer, the project or its domain, because this record is public and the shape is what generalises. The agent there wrote, via report_manual_work: "Four throwaway scripts this session — clone detection, the import-boundary walk, the nine-profile survey, the protocol enumeration — each answering a question the design was holding open. I logged the diagnosis as unknown rather than 'tool missing': reflow2 reads the design graph, not source trees, and whether it should is a real question, not an obvious gap. Guessing would have corrupted the signal."

THREE THINGS THIS SETTLES OR SHARPENS:

(1) ⭐ OPTION (b) OF THIS DECISION IS WORKING WITHOUT BEING BUILT. The question asks whether reflow2 needs an instrument to SEE hand-rolled work; its closing objection was that both prior findings surfaced by an agent noticing and saying so. This is the third instance, on a project reflow2's authors do not sit in, through the tool built for it (cap:a-session-reports-the-work-it-did-by-hand), unprompted, with a careful diagnosis. The negative space is being reported. What is still missing is on THIS side: nobody reads the reports back across designs, because they live in each consumer's own graph — Anthony had to relay this one by hand.

(2) THE CONVERSION TEST, run here 2026-09-14 (the wrench rule: ask find_tools the question a USER would ask, in their words):
  · "does my declared decomposition match the real coupling — walk the imports across the boundaries I declared" → top hits evaluate_allocation, detect_defects, realizes, seam_coverage. NONE of them walks source. ⭐ BUT THE ANSWER EXISTS: tools/wall_check.py, cap:a-declared-wall-is-checked-against-the-coupling-it-contains, built 2026-08-20 from the IDENTICAL hand-rolled script on reflow2's own design and generalised on Anthony's word to "any project, with no configuration". find_tools cannot return it because it is a script in reflow2's repo, not a served tool — and the consumer kit tarball carries only reflow2_init.py and getting-started/, so a project installed from the kit DOES NOT HAVE IT (fact:defect-the-wall-check-claims-any-project-and-ships-only-in-the-dev-repo). From where that agent stood, "unknown" was the honest diagnosis; from here, it is "built, unserved, and unshipped" — the same import-boundary question answered by hand for the SECOND time in 25 days, on a second project.
  · "find duplicated or cloned code" → find_tools, invalidated_findings, record_finding. Nothing. Not served.
  · "enumerate the protocols this system speaks at its boundaries" → add_actor, set_interface_designation, seam_coverage. The graph-side vocabulary for the ANSWER exists; nothing derives it from source. Not served.
  · "survey the configuration profiles the system is built in" → reconcile_deployment, deploy_to. Nothing reads a build's profiles. Not served.
  Score: 1 of 4 has a home, and that home is unreachable from a consumer; 3 of 4 have none.

(3) THE QUESTION THE AGENT REFUSED TO GUESS AT IS REAL AND IS NOT YET ON THE RECORD AS A DECISION: does reflow2 read source trees, or only the design that describes them? Today the honest answer is "one instrument does, deliberately, with no configuration, by reading Artifact locations off the graph — and it is not shipped." The three unserved analyses are all of that same shape: a question the DESIGN holds open whose evidence lives in SOURCE. wall_check's stated limit applies to all of them — an import graph is coupling, not a contract; a clone is similarity, not a duplicate; an enumerated protocol is a string, not a published boundary — so any of them, if built, reports and never writes back as design.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the agent's four questions were the design's most valuable open ones or merely the ones scriptable in an afternoon; the reports themselves were not read (they are in the consumer's graph), only the agent's summary of them.
